title: Runtime heap silting causing KV cache contamination and GPU OOMs in multi-tenant serving
creator: Ava Patel
description: Customer escalations across Hosted and Dedicated surfaced a recurring GPU OOM pattern during long-tail conversational loads. Root cause (preliminary): allocator 'silting' — small, fragmented free regions interleaved with large pinned KV cache pages prevented coalescing and triggered OOM under bursty requests with variable sequence lengths. The issue manifests as per-session KV handles growing without being reclaimed, kernel selection fallback thrashing, and slab fragmentation that prevents large contiguous allocations for attention state. Result: degraded availability for a small set of customers, elevated error rates, and two Sev2 pages in the last 10 days.
steps_to_reproduce: Run multi-tenant stress harness with mixed short/long sequences (1–4096 tokens) and intermittent cache pinning (simulate long-running chat sessions)
Enable continuous-batching with target latency SLOs and KV prefix caching turned on
Ramp to high concurrency (75% of pool capacity) and inject a subset of requests with large attn state to force allocations
Observe allocator free lists, slab fragmentation stats, and per-session KV handle counts in /metrics and logs
mitigation_actions: Immediate: deploy runtime flag to enable aggressive per-session KV eviction (canary to 5% of host pools in Hosted and single Dedicated region)
Immediate: add kernel-selection fallback lock to avoid repeated expensive kernel swaps under pressure
Emergency patch: background slab coalescer that runs every 30s to merge adjacent free slabs (hotfix PR referenced below)
Customer-facing: pushed incident notice, asked affected customers to accept temporary request-rate throttles; offered credits and prioritized Dedicated rescheduling
technical_analysis: Allocator currently uses mixed-size arenas with delayed coalescing; long-lived KV allocations create fragmentation 'islands' (we term this 'silting')
KV compaction path only runs on explicit eviction; under load the compactor is starved and per-session tombstones accumulate
Kernel-selection heuristics cause oscillation when a model switches between short/long paths leading to wasted memory reservations during kernel swap handoffs
In private deployments with older kernel drivers, page-size rounding worsened fragmentation and increased contiguous allocation failures
notes: Design review 2025-03-12: agreed to short-term slab coalescer + longer-term allocator redesign (buddy-style free lists)
QA: created deterministic replay harness for fragmentation scenarios; baseline before patch recorded 92% repro rate, after hotfix reduced to 6%
Performance: hotfix increases minor GC overhead ~1.8% p99 latency under synthetic load; acceptable for P0 rollout
Security: no customer data exposure seen; KV tombstones only referenced session ids — confirmed by security review on 2025-03-15
communications: Private customer update threads: Drive doc - https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a2b3c-kv-incident-summary
Posted follow-up in #cust-escalations with remediation ETA and mitigation steps
qa_and_rollout_plan: Canary (Hosted): 5% traffic with hotfix + eviction flag for 24h, monitor token-level OOMs and allocator metrics
Canary (Dedicated): single shard in us-west-2 with customer opt-in; run stress harness continuously for 48h
Private: provide patch bundle + manual upgrade instructions to customers; advise kernel driver check and suggest page-size tuning
Full rollout contingent on 48h stability and no regression in cost-per-token metric beyond target thresholds
code_review_feedback: @noah.rivera: prefer exponential backoff on coalescer to avoid steady CPU when fragmentation is low
@evie.singh: add unit tests for slab boundary conditions and intentional fragmentation sequences
@mike-g: confirm metrics tags for per-session eviction so Console can attribute impact to customers
postmortem_actions: Create regression suite for 'silting' patterns and fold into CI (runtime-stability/regression/silting-test)
Schedule allocator redesign spike (4 weeks) to evaluate buddy/free-list hybrid; proposal due 2025-04-15
Add telemetry: per-session KV age histogram, slab-coalescer runtimes, kernel-swap counters with model tags
Update runbook: add steps to enable per-session eviction and safe rollout playbook for Dedicated/Private
next_steps: Merge hotfix PRs after final security sign-off (security ok on 2025-03-15)
